name: Klingon
variety: the language of the published dictionary, in its romanisation
sources: Okrand, Marc (1992). The Klingon Dictionary, second edition.
contrasts: a glottal stop that ends syllables as well as begins them
allophony: p, t and q are aspirated; r is a trill

stress.rule: In a verb the stress falls on the stem; in a noun on the syllable that ends in a glottal stop, or on the stem.

rhythm.notes: No measurement exists: the class is what the design of the language implies.

intonation.declarative: not prescribed; speakers carry over the fall of their own languages
intonation.yes_no_question: marked by a suffix on the verb; melody not described
intonation.accent_shape: not prescribed; higher pitch on the stressed syllable is the usual practice
intonation.notes: The language has no native speakers whose melody could be described; what is given is the practice of its users.
